headline: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has declined, for now, to follow US President Donald Trump's call to rename artificial intelligence "superintelligence".
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; the reply is reported and shows an ally's position, but it changes no policy.
importance_line: It shows a close US ally declining to follow the US president's wording at once, which matters to governments and companies that write AI documents, but she left the door open by saying she will watch how other countries respond.
summary: Kyodo News reports that Takaichi told Japan's lower house of parliament on 8 Oct 2026 that "AI" is the right term for now, because it is used in government documents and academic papers and changing it everywhere at once would be hard, and that she would watch how other governments respond. She was answering Yuichiro Tamaki, leader of the Democratic Party for the People, about Trump's call in his UN General Assembly speech last month for the US government to use "SI" (superintelligence) in official documents; this edition also carries The Independent's 8 Oct report that Trump called people who say "artificial intelligence" "the enemy" (item C05-02).
notes: Reply story: Takaichi answers Trump's rename push. Seoul Economic Daily text is an AI translation from Korean crediting Kyodo, so wording of her answer is paraphrased. Original Kyodo piece not read. Freshness NEW because her reply is of 8 Oct 2026; Trump's UN speech was in Sept 2026 (exact date not given).
